title: Why "You Don't Lose Money Until You Sell" Is Bunk

agent_label.reasoning: Reference-backed (agent-proposed, pending owner confirmation): the article's claims are standard, correct finance principles -- mark-to-market defines a real unrealized loss, opportunity cost is symmetric, tax realization is distinct from value change, anchoring bias and tax-loss harvesting are well-established. See verdicts_agent_proposed.json for per-claim verdicts.

claims.claim_text: a decline from $100k to $78k is a real $22k loss in current value whether or not the position is sold (mark-to-market)
selling forgoes future appreciation/income while also avoiding further potential loss (opportunity cost is symmetric)
selling changes tax status (realizes a gain/loss) but that is separate from whether value was actually lost
the phrase encourages anchoring to purchase price rather than market price (anchoring bias)
believing losses aren't real until sale makes investors hold underperformers longer, risking deeper losses
the mindset discourages tax-loss harvesting that could cut taxes while keeping market exposure
